text.p: A rise in Spanish bond prices and a stronger escudo pushed Portuguese futures higher and lent some support to sluggish cash bonds.

"If the escudo goes higher against the mark on the back of the dollar's rise that could breathe some life into cash maturities of up to five years," said one trader. "Ten-year bonds are likely to stay stuck in a tight range."
Dealers said profit-taking could inhibit further gains in the futures market.
Overnight/tomorrow next rates firmed to 6.10/6.25 percent from 6.00/6.10 percent last week.
Traders said there was resistance to gains on the futures, and if the contract rose further it could attract profit-taking.

The 10-year cash was also unlikely to go much below 90 basis points with Germany, they added. More potential upside was seen at the shorter end of the curve up to five years, particularly if the escudo gained on the mark.

The steadiness of the escudo should induce fresh talk of a rate cut in the short term, traders said. "The year-on-year CPI (inflation) is going to go below two percent this month, what was missing was a calm and strong escudo," said one trader.
